title: Storyboard
skill: Plan before you generate. No AI this week.

teacher.warmUp: Show a comic page next to its storyboard. What did the artist decide before drawing?
teacher.miniLesson: Show how to split a story into pages and panels: one moment per panel, and what the camera sees (close-up or wide shot). Sketch one panel on the board with stick figures and write its dialogue underneath.
teacher.studio: On paper, children split their story into pages and panels, sketch each panel with stick figures and write the dialogue. Ages 8–9: 4 pages of 3 panels. Ages 10–11: 6 to 8 pages of 3 to 5 panels. Their board on the platform shows their hero, characters, places and story from earlier weeks.
teacher.shareSave: Partners swap storyboards: can you follow the story without the words? Children keep their storyboard for next week.

kid.intro: No AI this week! Real comic artists plan on paper first. Your board shows everything you’ve made so far.
steps: Look at your board: your hero, friends, places and story.
On paper, split your story into pages and panels.
Sketch each panel with stick figures.
Write what each character says under each panel.
kid.starterPrompt: No AI this week: grab your pencil!

steps: Look at your board: your hero, your sidekick, your places and your story.
On paper, split your story into 4 pages of 3 panels.
Sketch each panel with stick figures.
Write what each character says under each panel.
Look at your board: your hero, your sidekick, your villain, your places and your story.
On paper, split your story into 6 to 8 pages of 3 to 5 panels.
Sketch each panel with stick figures and choose close-ups or wide shots.
Write the dialogue and narration under each panel.

ai.systemPrompt: This is a paper week: there is no AI helper.
